claim: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) affects one in ~4000 people worldwide.
source: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is an inherited retinal degenerative disease that affects one in ~4000 people worldwide (Hartong et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hartong et al., 2006

claim: RP first manifests as poor night vision.
source: The disease first manifests as poor night vision, likely due to the fact that many RP disease genes are expressed in rod photoreceptors, which initiate night vision.
evidence: Based on established clinical knowledge about RP presentation

claim: Many RP disease genes are expressed in rod photoreceptors.
source: The disease first manifests as poor night vision, likely due to the fact that many RP disease genes are expressed in rod photoreceptors, which initiate night vision.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about RP genetics

claim: Cone photoreceptors are affected in RP.
source: Cone photoreceptors, which are required for daylight, color, and high acuity vision, also are affected, as are the retina-pigmented epithelial (RPE) cells (Chrenek et al., 2012; Napoli et al., 2021; Napoli and Strettoi, 2023; Wu et al., 2021), which support both rod and cone photoreceptors.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: RPE cells are affected in RP.
source: Cone photoreceptors, which are required for daylight, color, and high acuity vision, also are affected, as are the retina-pigmented epithelial (RPE) cells (Chrenek et al., 2012; Napoli et al., 2021; Napoli and Strettoi, 2023; Wu et al., 2021), which support both rod and cone photoreceptors.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Cones and RPE cells typically do not express RP disease genes.
source: However, cones and RPE cells typically do not express RP disease genes.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about RP gene expression patterns

claim: RP cones lose function and die after most of the rods in their immediate neighborhood die.
source: Nonetheless, RP cones lose function and die after most of the rods in their immediate neighborhood die.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about RP disease progression

claim: Problems with metabolism, oxidative stress, lack of trophic factors, oversupply of chromophore, and inflammation may cause cone death in RP.
source: While it is not entirely clear what causes cone death, there are data suggesting problems with metabolism, oxidative stress, lack of trophic factors, oversupply of chromophore, and inflammation (Komeima et al., 2006; Mohand-Said et al., 1998; Punzo et al., 2009; Xue et al., 2023; Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: RP cones do not have enough glucose, their main fuel source.
source: Several lines of evidence suggest that RP cones do not have enough glucose, their main fuel source (Reviewed in Xue and Cepko, 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to a review

claim: Overexpression of TXNIP prolonged the survival of cones and cone-mediated vision in three RP mouse strains.
source: We found that overexpression of TXNIP, an α-arrestin protein with multiple functions, including glucose metabolism, prolonged the survival of cones and cone-mediated vision in three RP mouse strains (Xue et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: TXNIP rescue of cones relied upon the utilization of lactate by cones.
source: Regarding the mechanism of rescue, we found that it relied upon the utilization of lactate by cones.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Xue et al., 2021)

claim: Cones treated with Txnip showed improved mitochondrial morphology and function.
source: In addition, cones treated with Txnip showed improved mitochondrial morphology and function.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Xue et al., 2021)

claim: TXNIP is known to bind directly to thioredoxin.
source: As TXNIP is known to bind directly to thioredoxin, we tested a Txnip allele with a single amino acid (aa) change, C247S, which abolishes the interaction with thioredoxin (Patwari et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: The C247S mutation abolishes the interaction between TXNIP and thioredoxin.
source: As TXNIP is known to bind directly to thioredoxin, we tested a Txnip allele with a single amino acid (aa) change, C247S, which abolishes the interaction with thioredoxin (Patwari et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: The Txnip C247S allele provided better rescue than the wild-type Txnip allele.
source: This allele provided better rescue than the wild-type (wt) Txnip allele, ruling out its interaction with thioredoxin as required for cone rescue.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Xue et al., 2021)

claim: The interaction between TXNIP and thioredoxin is not required for cone rescue.
source: This allele provided better rescue than the wild-type (wt) Txnip allele, ruling out its interaction with thioredoxin as required for cone rescue.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that C247S provides better rescue

claim: ARRDC4 shares ~60% similar amino acids with TXNIP.
source: Among them, arrestin domain-containing protein 4 (ARRDC4) is the closest to TXNIP in amino acid sequence, sharing ~60% similar amino acids with TXNIP (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 1A

claim: ARRDC4 is thought to have functions similar to TXNIP in regulating glucose metabolism in vitro.
source: ARRDC4 is thought to have functions that are similar to those of TXNIP in regulating glucose metabolism in vitro (Patwari et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: ARRDC4 is composed of three domains: a N-terminal arrestin domain, a C-terminal arrestin domain, and an intrinsically disordered region (IDR) at the C-terminus.
source: Like TXNIP and other α-arrestins, ARRDC4 is composed of three domains: a N-terminal arrestin (Arrestin N-) domain, a C-terminal arrestin (Arrestin C-) domain, and an intrinsically disordered region (IDR) at the C-terminus.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about α-arrestin structure

claim: Previous crystallography studies did not reveal the full structure of the TXNIP protein due to the IDR lacking a stable 3D structure.
source: Because an IDR lacks a stable 3D structure under physiological conditions, previous studies using crystallography did not reveal the full structure of the TXNIP protein (Hwang et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: ARRDC4 is predicted to have a 'W' shaped arrestin structure composed of the Arrestin N- and C-domains, plus a long IDR which looks like a tail.
source: Similar to TXNIP, ARRDC4 is predicted to have a 'W' shaped arrestin structure, which is composed of the Arrestin N- and C-domains, plus a long IDR which looks like a tail (Figure 1B).
evidence: Based on AlphaFold-2 prediction shown in Figure 1B

claim: Expression of Arrdc4 in rd1 cones resulted in much lower cone counts relative to the control.
source: Unlike Txnip, the cone counts were much lower in Arrdc4 treated retina relative to the AAV-H2BGFP control (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C and D

claim: Overexpressing the Txnip wt allele in the RPE using an RPE-specific promoter did not improve RP cone survival.
source: We previously showed (Xue et al., 2021) that overexpressing the Txnip wt allele in the RPE using an RPE-specific promoter, derived from the human BEST1 gene (Esumi et al., 2009), did not improve RP cone survival.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: The wt Txnip allele removes the glucose transporter from the plasma membrane.
source: The wt allele removes the glucose transporter from the plasma membrane, thus preventing the RPE from taking up glucose for its own metabolism, and preventing it from serving as a conduit for glucose to flow from the blood to the cones.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about TXNIP function

claim: The triple mutant Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA improved cone survival when expressed only in the RPE.
source: However, a triple mutant, Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA, improved cone survival when expressed only in the RPE (Xue et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: The LL351 and 352AA mutations eliminate a clathrin-binding site required for Txnip's interaction with clathrin-coated pits for removal of GLUT1 from the cell surface.
source: The LL351 and 352AA mutations eliminate a clathrin-binding site, which is required for Txnip's interaction with clathrin-coated pits for removal of GLUT1 from the cell surface (Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: The RPE normally uses lactate in wt animals.
source: Although the RPE normally uses lactate in wt animals, in RP, it is hypothesized that it retains the glucose that it normally would deliver to cones (Reviewed in Hurley, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to a review

claim: In RP, the RPE is hypothesized to retain glucose that it normally would deliver to cones.
source: Although the RPE normally uses lactate in wt animals, in RP, it is hypothesized that it retains the glucose that it normally would deliver to cones (Reviewed in Hurley, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to a review

claim: The retention of glucose by the RPE in RP is thought to be due to a reduction in lactate supply from rods.
source: The retention of glucose by the RPE is thought to be due to a reduction in lactate supply, as rods normally provide lactate for the RPE, and with rod loss that source would be greatly diminished.
evidence: Based on inference from known metabolic relationships

claim: Rods normally provide lactate for the RPE.
source: The retention of glucose by the RPE is thought to be due to a reduction in lactate supply, as rods normally provide lactate for the RPE, and with rod loss that source would be greatly diminished.
evidence: Based on established knowledge about retinal metabolism

claim: The rd1 retina in the FVB strain shows holes in the cone layer, which appear as 'craters.'
source: In addition, the rd1 retina in the FVB strain used here, even without any treatment, shows holes in the cone layer, which appear as 'craters.'
evidence: Based on observation in this study

claim: An RP rat model presents a similar pattern of craters.
source: An RP rat model presents a similar pattern (Ji et al., 2014; Ji et al., 2012; Zhu et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations

claim: When Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA are expressed in the RPE, there are more craters in the photoreceptor layer.
source: When Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA are expressed in the RPE, there are more craters in the photoreceptor layer.
evidence: Based on observation in this study

claim: The N-terminus of TXNIP is sufficient to interact with KPNA2 for TXNIP's localization to the nucleus.
source: For example, the N-terminus is sufficient to interact with KPNA2 for TXNIP's localization to the nucleus (Nishinaka et al., 2004), while the C-terminus of TXNIP is critical for interactions with COPS5, to inhibit cancer cell proliferation (Jeon et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: The C-terminus of TXNIP is critical for interactions with COPS5 to inhibit cancer cell proliferation.
source: For example, the N-terminus is sufficient to interact with KPNA2 for TXNIP's localization to the nucleus (Nishinaka et al., 2004), while the C-terminus of TXNIP is critical for interactions with COPS5, to inhibit cancer cell proliferation (Jeon et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: The C-terminus of TXNIP is necessary for inhibition of glycolysis in vitro.
source: The C-terminus of TXNIP is also necessary for inhibition of glycolysis, at least in vitro, through an unclear mechanism (Patwari et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: When an AAV that expressed in the RPE was co-injected with AAV8-RedO-H2BGFP-WPRE-bGHpA, H2BGFP was expressed in the RPE, along with expression in cones.
source: However, when an AAV that expressed in the RPE, i.e., AAV8-Best1-Sv40intron-(Gene)-WPRE-bGHpA, was co-injected with AAV8-RedO-H2BGFP-WPRE-bGHpA, H2BGFP was expressed in the RPE, along with expression in cones (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A

claim: The expression of H2BGFP in the RPE when co-injected with an RPE-expressing AAV is speculated to be due to concatenation or recombination of the two genomes.
source: We speculate that this is due to concatenation or recombination of the two genomes, such that the H2BGFP comes under the control of the RPE promoter.
evidence: Based on speculation about the mechanism

claim: The AAV genome copy number was ~10 fold lower in cones than in the RPE.
source: It was previously observed that the AAV genome copy number was »10 fold lower in cones than in the RPE (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: The 149-397aa portion of Txnip.C247S (C.Txnip.C247S) had the highest activity for GLUT1 removal from the RPE basal surface in vivo.
source: The 149-397aa portion of Txnip.C247S (C.Txnip.C247S) had the highest activity for GLUT1 removal from the RPE basal surface in vivo, while the 1-228aa portion (N.Txnip) failed to remove GLUT1 (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: The 1-228aa portion of TXNIP (N.Txnip) failed to remove GLUT1 from the RPE basal surface.
source: The 149-397aa portion of Txnip.C247S (C.Txnip.C247S) had the highest activity for GLUT1 removal from the RPE basal surface in vivo, while the 1-228aa portion (N.Txnip) failed to remove GLUT1 (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: The Arrestin C-domain of TXNIP interacts with the intracellular C-terminal IDR of GLUT1.
source: As predicted by ColabFold, an AI algorithm based on AlphaFold-2 (Mirdita et al., 2022), the Arrestin C-domain, which is part of C.Txnip.C247S, but is not present in the N-domain of TXNIP, interacts with the intracellular C-terminal IDR of GLUT1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Based on AI prediction shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2

claim: The C-terminal portion of TXNIP is sufficient to bind and clear GLUT1 from cell surface, while the N-domain is not.
source: These results are consistent with these predictions, in that the C-terminal portion of TXNIP is sufficient to bind and clear GLUT1 from cell surface, while the N-domain is not.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results and AI predictions

claim: Best1-Txnip.C247S did not show significant improvement of cone survival.
source: Similar to Best1-wt Txnip (Xue et al., 2021), Best1-Txnip.C247S did not show significant improvement of cone survival, ruling out the C247S mutation alone as promoting the cone survival by Best1-Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2

claim: The C247S mutation alone does not promote cone survival when TXNIP is expressed in the RPE.
source: Similar to Best1-wt Txnip (Xue et al., 2021), Best1-Txnip.C247S did not show significant improvement of cone survival, ruling out the C247S mutation alone as promoting the cone survival by Best1-Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results

claim: Best1-N.Txnip (1-228aa) and Best1-sC.Txnip (255-397aa) failed to improve cone survival.
source: In addition, Best1-N.Txnip (1-228aa) and Best1-sC.Txnip (255-397aa, sC: short C-) failed to improve cone survival.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2

claim: Best1-C.Txnip.C247S (149-397aa), Best1-C.Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA (149-397aa), and Best1-nt.Txnip.C247S320 (1-320aa) promoted significant cone survival compared to the corresponding control retinas.
source: However, Best1-C.Txnip.C247S (149-397aa), Best1-C.Txnip.C247S.LL351 and 352AA (149-397aa), and Best1-nt.Txnip.C247S320 (1-320aa, nt: no-tail) promoted significant cone survival compared to the corresponding control retinas.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2

claim: Best1-N.Txnip and Best1-sC.Txnip-treated rd1 retina did not have increased numbers of craters.
source: Best1-N.Txnip and Best1-sC.Txnip-treated rd1 retina did not have increased numbers of craters, while all other vectors increased the number of craters.
evidence: Based on observation in this study

claim: All vectors except Best1-N.Txnip and Best1-sC.Txnip increased the number of craters in rd1 retina.
source: Best1-N.Txnip and Best1-sC.Txnip-treated rd1 retina did not have increased numbers of craters, while all other vectors increased the number of craters.
evidence: Based on observation in this study

claim: The C-terminal portion of TXNIP expressed in the RPE is required for RP cone survival, for a function(s) that is unrelated to the removal of GLUT1, or to the mechanism that leads to an increase in craters.
source: These results suggest that the C-terminal portion of TXNIP expressed in the RPE is required for RP cone survival, for a function(s) that is unrelated to the removal of GLUT1, or to the mechanism that leads to an increase in craters.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results

claim: Neither N.Txnip (1-228aa) nor C.Txnip.C247S (149-397aa) promoted significant improvement in rd1 cone survival when expressed in cones.
source: Neither N.Txnip (1-228aa) nor C.Txnip.C247S (149-397aa) promoted significant improvement in rd1 cone survival.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3

claim: nt.Tnxip.C247S301 (1-301aa) and nt.Txnip.C247S320 (1-320aa) promoted survival of rd1 cones: 47% and 63% more cones than the control GFP virus, respectively.
source: However, nt.Tnxip.C247S301 (1-301aa) and nt.Txnip.C247S320 (1-320aa) promoted survival of rd1 cones: 47% and 63% more cones than the control GFP virus, respectively (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B

claim: The full-length Txnip.C247S promoted an increase of 97% in cones.
source: In comparison, the full-length Txnip.C247S promoted an increase of 97% in cones in our previous study (Xue et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: The full-length Txnip provides the most benefit in terms of RP cone survival when expressed in cones.
source: These results show that the full-length Txnip provides the most benefit in terms of RP cone survival.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of experimental results

claim: CMV-Txnip.C247S provided a 38% rescue.
source: CMV-Txnip.C247S provided a 38% rescue (Figure 3A and C), which is lower than RedO-Txnip.C247S (97%) alone.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and C

claim: CMV-Txnip.C247S rescue (38%) is lower than RedO-Txnip.C247S (97%) alone.
source: CMV-Txnip.C247S provided a 38% rescue (Figure 3A and C), which is lower than RedO-Txnip.C247S (97%) alone.
evidence: Based on comparison of experimental results

claim: PARP1 mutants have been shown to protect mitochondria under stress.
source: PARP1 mutants have been shown to protect mitochondria under stress (Hocsak et al., 2017; Szczesny et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations

claim: PARP1 knock-out did not provide cone rescue in rd1 mice.
source: Accordingly, in our previous study, we crossed the null PARP1 mice with rd1 mice, to ask if mitochondrial improvements alone were sufficient to induce cone rescue. We found that it was not.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Xue et al., 2021)

claim: HSP90AB1 inhibition improved skeletal muscle mitochondrial metabolism in a diabetes mouse model.
source: In our current study, we thus prioritized HSP90AB1 inhibition, which had been shown to improve skeletal muscle mitochondrial metabolism in a diabetes mouse model (Jing et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: All three shRNAs targeting Hsp90ab1 reduced the HSP90AB1-FLAG signal compared to the shNC control.
source: All three shRNAs reduced the HSP90AB1-FLAG signal compared to the shNC, the non-targeting control shRNA (Figure 5A and B), suggesting that they are able to inhibit the expression of HSP90AB1 protein in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and B

claim: shHsp90ab1(#a) and shHsp90ab1(#c) increased the survival of rd1 cones at P50.
source: The two shRNAs with the most activity in reducing the FLAG-tagged HSP90AB1 signal, shHsp90ab1(#a), and shHsp90ab1(#c), were found to increase the survival of rd1 cones at P50 (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and D

claim: A slight additive effect of shHsp90ab1 and Txnip.C247S was observed.
source: A slight additive effect of shHsp90ab1 and Txnip.C247S was observed (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E and F

claim: The knock-down of Hsp90ab1 did not provide rescue effect on a Parp1 loss of function background.
source: We also asked if there might be an effect of the knock-down of Hsp90ab1 on a Parp1 loss of function background. We did not observe any rescue effect of the shRNAs on this background (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G and H

claim: Txnip has different mechanisms for Txnip-mediated cone survival when expressed in the RPE versus in cones.
source: The results suggest that Txnip has different mechanisms for Txnip-mediated cone survival when expressed in the RPE versus in cones.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results

claim: The C-terminal portion of Txnip.C247S (149-397aa) expressed within the RPE, but not within cones, delayed the degeneration of cones.
source: The C-terminal portion of Txnip.C247S (149-397aa) expressed within the RPE, but not within cones, delayed the degeneration of cones (Figure 2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2

claim: The full-length Txnip.C247S expressed within cones, but not within the RPE, was the most effective configuration for cone survival.
source: The full-length Txnip.C247S expressed within cones, but not within the RPE, was the most effective configuration for cone survival (Figure 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3

claim: The expression of full-length Txnip.C247S in both the RPE and cones did not provide better rescue than in cones alone.
source: The expression of full-length Txnip.C247S in both the RPE and cones did not provide better rescue than in cones alone.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3

claim: The N-terminal half of TXNIP (1-228aa) might exert harmful effects in the RPE that negate the beneficial effects from the C-terminal half.
source: The N-terminal half of TXNIP (1-228aa) might exert harmful effects in the RPE, that negate the beneficial effects from the C-terminal half, suggested by the observation that its removal, in the C-terminal 149–397 allele, led to better cone survival when expressed in the RPE (Figure 2).
evidence: Inferred from experimental results shown in Figure 2

claim: In cones, the C-terminal half of TXNIP, including the C-terminal IDR tail, may cooperate with the N-terminal half, or negate its negative effects, to benefit RP cone survival.
source: In cones, the C-terminal half, including the C-terminal IDR tail, may cooperate with the N-terminal half, or negate its negative effects, to benefit RP cone survival.
evidence: Speculative interpretation of experimental results

claim: The C-terminal half of TXNIP is not sufficient for cone rescue when expressed in cones, as the 149–397 allele did not rescue.
source: However, the C-terminal half is not sufficient for cone rescue when expressed in cones, as the 149–397 allele did not rescue.

claim: The 149–397 allele of TXNIP rescues cones when expressed in the RPE, but not when expressed in cones.

claim: The 149–397 allele loses cone rescue activity if it loses aa 149–254, when expressed in the RPE, as shown by the 255–397 allele.
source: This domain loses the cone rescue activity if it loses aa 149–254, when expressed in the RPE, as shown by the 255–397 allele.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2

claim: In cones, the rescue activity is present in the 1–301 and the 1–320 allele, but is lost in the 149–397 allele.
source: In cones, the rescue activity is present in the 1–301 and the 1–320 allele, but is lost in the 149–397 allele.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3

claim: The LLAA TXNIP mutant is unable to effectively remove the glucose transporter due to its loss of interaction with clathrin.
source: The LLAA TXNIP mutant is unable to effectively remove the transporter, due to its loss of interaction with clathrin (Wu et al., 2013).

claim: When the LLAA mutant allele is expressed in the RPE, it leads to improved cone survival, in contrast to the wt allele.
source: When this mutant allele is expressed in the RPE, it leads to improved cone survival, in contrast to the wt allele.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work (Xue et al., 2021)

claim: When the LLAA allele is expressed in cones, it promotes cone survival, though not as well as the wt allele.
source: When the LLAA allele is expressed in cones, it also promotes cone survival, though not as well as the wt allele (Xue et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: The wt TXNIP allele might be more beneficial in cones if it is part of the mechanism that forces cones to rely more heavily on lactate vs. glucose.
source: The wt allele might be more beneficial in cones if it is part of the mechanism that forces cones to rely more heavily on lactate vs. glucose.

claim: TXNIP has unique functions that protect RP cones.
source: This observation suggests that TXNIP has unique functions that protect RP cones.

claim: The activation of the insulin/mTORC1 pathway is beneficial to RP cone survival.
source: The implication of this potential role regarding RP cone survival is unclear, but interestingly, the activation of the insulin/mTORC1 pathway is beneficial to RP cone survival (Punzo et al., 2009; Venkatesh et al., 2015).

claim: The interaction of TXNIP with thioredoxin is apparently negative for cone survival.

claim: The release of thioredoxin from TXNIP allows it to play its anti-oxidation role, which would be important in the RP retina which exhibits oxidative damage.

claim: HSP90AB1 interacts with both the wt and C247S alleles of TXNIP.

claim: Inhibiting HSP90AA1 with small molecules transiently delayed cone death in human retinal organoids under low glucose conditions.

claim: TXNIP-mediated rescue does not rely upon PARP1.

claim: TXNIP is an α-arrestin protein.

evidence: Based on established knowledge about α-arrestin structure

claim: An IDR lacks a stable 3D structure under physiological conditions.
